title: AEGS Incident Record
description:
Something went wrong, or nearly did. AEGS requires that incidents be recordable as first-class objects rather than inferred from logs, because the events that matter most -- a control that failed, a refusal that was overridden, a vulnerability found -- are exactly the ones a log written by the failing system is least likely to describe well.

A near-miss is an incident. An attack that was refused is worth recording as much as one that succeeded, because the difference is often luck.

affected.description: Decision, authorization or agent ids involved.

detectedBy.description: Which control, test or person found it. 'A red-team run' is a legitimate answer and a good sign.

wasRefused.description: Whether the action was stopped. A near-miss is still an incident.

refusedByExpectedControl.description: False means it was stopped by luck rather than by the control that should have stopped it -- a finding, not a pass.

residualRisk.description: What remains after mitigation. 'None' is rarely true and should be justified.
